CMS Synthetic Data (DE-SynPUF) — Chronic Condition & Cost Analysis

Ann Raymond

2026-10-05

1. Overview

This notebook picks up where cms_synpuf_cleaning.Rmd leaves off: it reads four of the five cleaned CSVs that notebook saves to Data/Clean/ (Beneficiary, Inpatient, Outpatient, and PDE; Carrier isn’t used here) and does three pieces of downstream analysis on them —

  1. Chronic Condition Prevalence & Correlations — how common each of the 11 CMS-flagged chronic conditions is, and a heatmap of their pairwise correlations.
  2. Claim Costs by Chronic Condition — total claim amounts across all payers for Inpatient, Outpatient, and Prescription Drug Event claims, among beneficiaries with each condition (joined to the Beneficiary file’s condition flags).
  3. Reconciling Beneficiary Annual Amounts Against Claims — whether the Beneficiary file’s annual reimbursement totals tie out against what’s actually in the Inpatient/Outpatient claims files, using CMS’s own documented derivation formulas.

It does not re-pull or re-clean anything — if the CSVs in Data/Clean/ aren’t there yet (or are stale), run cms_synpuf_cleaning.Rmd first.

2. Setup & load cleaned data

required_pkgs <- c("tidyverse", "lubridate", "data.table")

installed <- rownames(installed.packages())
missing <- setdiff(required_pkgs, installed)
if (length(missing) > 0) {
  install.packages(missing, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(data.table)

Beneficiary and Inpatient are small enough to read whole with readr. Outpatient (75 columns, 780K rows) and PDE (8 columns, 5.6M rows) are read with data.table::fread() and select = to pull only the columns this notebook actually uses — no reason to load 70 unused diagnosis/procedure columns just to compute a cost summary.

beneficiary_all <- read_csv("../Data/Clean/beneficiary_2008_2010.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

inpatient_clean <- read_csv("../Data/Clean/inpatient_claims_sample_1.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

outpatient_clean <- fread(
  "../Data/Clean/outpatient_claims_sample_1.csv",
  select = c("beneficiary_id", "claim_end_date", "medicare_payment_amt",
             "beneficiary_blood_deductible_amt", "beneficiary_part_b_deductible_amt",
             "beneficiary_part_b_coinsurance_amt", "primary_payer_paid_amt", "total_claim_amt")
) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(claim_end_date = ymd(claim_end_date))

pde_clean <- fread(
  "../Data/Clean/prescription_drug_events_sample_1.csv",
  select = c("beneficiary_id", "gross_drug_cost_amt")
) %>%
  as_tibble()

cat("beneficiary_all:", nrow(beneficiary_all), "rows x", ncol(beneficiary_all), "cols\n")
## beneficiary_all: 343644 rows x 34 cols
cat("inpatient_clean:", nrow(inpatient_clean), "rows x", ncol(inpatient_clean), "cols\n")
## inpatient_clean: 66705 rows x 37 cols
cat("outpatient_clean (narrowed):", nrow(outpatient_clean), "rows x", ncol(outpatient_clean), "cols\n")
## outpatient_clean (narrowed): 779537 rows x 8 cols
cat("pde_clean (narrowed):", nrow(pde_clean), "rows x", ncol(pde_clean), "cols\n")
## pde_clean (narrowed): 5552421 rows x 2 cols

3. Chronic Condition Prevalence & Correlations

chronic_condition_count (computed in the cleaning notebook) is a simple row-sum across the 11 chronic_* flags. This section shows how common each condition is, then which conditions tend to occur together. It collapses to one row per beneficiary first (a condition counts as present if it was ever flagged TRUE in 2008, 2009, or 2010) — otherwise a chronic condition that persists across all three years would be counted three times for no real reason.

condition_cols <- c("chronic_alzheimer", "chronic_heart_failure", "chronic_kidney_disease",
                     "chronic_cancer", "chronic_copd", "chronic_depression", "chronic_diabetes",
                     "chronic_ischemic_heart_disease", "chronic_osteoporosis",
                     "chronic_rheumatoid_or_osteoarthritis", "chronic_stroke_tia")

bene_conditions_ever <- beneficiary_all %>%
  group_by(beneficiary_id) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(condition_cols), any), .groups = "drop")

cat("Unique beneficiaries across 3 years:", nrow(bene_conditions_ever), "\n")
## Unique beneficiaries across 3 years: 116352

Prevalence

How many beneficiaries have each condition, and what share of all beneficiaries that is — a sense of scale before looking at how conditions relate to each other.

tibble(
  condition = condition_cols,
  n_beneficiaries = colSums(bene_conditions_ever[condition_cols]),
  pct_of_beneficiaries = n_beneficiaries / nrow(bene_conditions_ever) * 100
) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_beneficiaries)) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
               caption = sprintf("Prevalence of each chronic condition (ever flagged in 2008-2010), out of %s beneficiaries",
                                 format(nrow(bene_conditions_ever), big.mark = ",")))

Pairwise correlations

All 11 inputs are 0/1, so a Pearson correlation here is the phi coefficient — a standard, well-defined measure of association for binary variables.

cond_matrix <- bene_conditions_ever %>%
  select(all_of(condition_cols)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>%
  as.matrix()

cor_matrix <- cor(cond_matrix)
cor_long <- cor_matrix %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("condition_1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-condition_1, names_to = "condition_2", values_to = "correlation")

ggplot(cor_long, aes(condition_1, condition_2, fill = correlation)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(correlation, 2)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", midpoint = 0) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), axis.title = element_blank()) +
  labs(title = "Chronic condition correlation matrix")

Worth flagging: CMS’s own FAQ says disclosure-limitation synthesis distorts these statistics — “much of the interdependence and co-variation among variables have been altered… univariate and multivariate statistics, such as conditional correlations and regression coefficients, would not be reliable.” Treat the prevalence figures and correlations above as a demonstration of the method, not as real clinical prevalence or comorbidity patterns (see Section 5 for the same caveat applied to dollar amounts).

4. Claim Costs by Chronic Condition

This section measures the total amount of each claim across all payers (Medicare, primary payer, and beneficiary responsibility), for beneficiaries who carry each condition. Inpatient, Outpatient, and PDE claims are joined to the condition flags from Section 3 (ever flagged). The amounts are for all of a beneficiary’s claims, not only claims attributable to the condition itself.

A beneficiary with 3 conditions contributes their claims to all 3 disease rows below — that’s deliberate (they are flagged with every one of those conditions), but it means claims are double- or triple-counted across condition rows, and the per-disease numbers are not independent samples of each other.

How each claim amount is built, per Codebook Appendix 2 (“List of Reimbursement Variables”):

Claim type Total claim amount (all payers)
Inpatient total_claim_amt = medicare_payment_amt + utilization_day_count × pass_through_per_diem_amt + primary_payer_paid_amt + Part A deductible + Part A coinsurance + blood deductible
Outpatient total_claim_amt = medicare_payment_amt + primary_payer_paid_amt + blood deductible + Part B deductible + Part B coinsurance
PDE gross_drug_cost_amt (ingredient cost + dispensing fee + sales tax + vaccine administration fee)

Inpatient includes the per-diem term because it is part of Medicare’s payment on those claims. Blank deductibles are treated as $0 in total_claim_amt, so all inpatient claims are included. PDE’s gross drug cost is already the total drug cost regardless of who pays, so the patient-pay amount is part of it and isn’t added again.

inpatient_claim_amts <- inpatient_clean %>%
  select(beneficiary_id, claim_amt = total_claim_amt)

outpatient_claim_amts <- outpatient_clean %>%
  select(beneficiary_id, claim_amt = total_claim_amt)

pde_claim_amts <- pde_clean %>%
  transmute(beneficiary_id, claim_amt = as.numeric(gross_drug_cost_amt))
condition_flags_long <- bene_conditions_ever %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(condition_cols), names_to = "condition", values_to = "has_condition") %>%
  filter(has_condition) %>%
  select(beneficiary_id, condition)
cost_ip <- condition_flags_long %>%
  inner_join(inpatient_claim_amts, by = "beneficiary_id", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(avg_inpatient_claim_amt = mean(claim_amt, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_inpatient_claim_amt = median(claim_amt, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_inpatient_claims = sum(!is.na(claim_amt)), .groups = "drop")

cost_op <- condition_flags_long %>%
  inner_join(outpatient_claim_amts, by = "beneficiary_id", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(avg_outpatient_claim_amt = mean(claim_amt, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_outpatient_claim_amt = median(claim_amt, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_outpatient_claims = sum(!is.na(claim_amt)), .groups = "drop")

PDE is 5.6M rows, and joining it fans out further still (a beneficiary’s prescriptions × however many conditions they carry), so this one uses data.table the same way Carrier Claims does in the cleaning notebook, to keep it fast and light on memory:

cost_pde <- merge(
  as.data.table(condition_flags_long),
  as.data.table(pde_claim_amts),
  by = "beneficiary_id", allow.cartesian = TRUE
)[, .(avg_prescription_claim_amt = mean(claim_amt, na.rm = TRUE),
      median_prescription_claim_amt = median(claim_amt, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_prescriptions = sum(!is.na(claim_amt))), by = condition] %>%
  as_tibble()
cost_by_disease <- cost_ip %>%
  full_join(cost_op, by = "condition") %>%
  full_join(cost_pde, by = "condition") %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_inpatient_claim_amt))

cost_by_disease %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
               caption = "Average & median total claim amount (all payers) per claim, among beneficiaries with each chronic condition")

5. Reconciling Beneficiary Annual Amounts Against Claims

Do annual_medicare_reimb_ip / annual_beneficiary_resp_ip / annual_primary_payer_reimb_ip (and the OP equivalents) in the Beneficiary file equal what you get by summing the matching claim-level amounts for that beneficiary-year? The Codebook’s Appendix 2 (“List of Reimbursement Variables”) spells out CMS’s exact derivation formulas, so this check uses those instead of a naive sum(medicare_payment_amt):

Beneficiary variable CMS’s stated derivation (Codebook Appendix 2)
annual_medicare_reimb_ip medicare_payment_amt + utilization_day_count * pass_through_per_diem_amt
annual_beneficiary_resp_ip beneficiary_deductible_amt + beneficiary_part_a_coinsurance_amt + beneficiary_blood_deductible_amt
annual_primary_payer_reimb_ip primary_payer_paid_amt
annual_medicare_reimb_op medicare_payment_amt
annual_beneficiary_resp_op beneficiary_blood_deductible_amt + beneficiary_part_b_deductible_amt + beneficiary_part_b_coinsurance_amt
annual_primary_payer_reimb_op primary_payer_paid_amt

(Carrier’s equivalents are also in Appendix 2, but conditional on LINE_PRCSG_IND_CD — a per-line processing-indicator code dropped during the Carrier collapse in the cleaning notebook. Reconciling Carrier would mean re-deriving it from the raw files, which is out of scope here — matching what was actually asked: Inpatient and Outpatient only.)

Claims are assigned to a calendar year using claim_end_date (raw CLM_THRU_DT), per the DUG’s own footnote to Table 1: “Year is determined by the claim through date.”

ip_by_bene_year <- inpatient_clean %>%
  mutate(claim_year = year(claim_end_date)) %>%
  group_by(beneficiary_id, reference_year = claim_year) %>%
  summarise(
    claims_medicare_ip = sum(medicare_payment_amt + utilization_day_count * pass_through_per_diem_amt, na.rm = TRUE),
    claims_benres_ip = sum(beneficiary_deductible_amt + beneficiary_part_a_coinsurance_amt + beneficiary_blood_deductible_amt, na.rm = TRUE),
    claims_pppymt_ip = sum(primary_payer_paid_amt, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

op_by_bene_year <- outpatient_clean %>%
  mutate(claim_year = year(claim_end_date)) %>%
  group_by(beneficiary_id, reference_year = claim_year) %>%
  summarise(
    claims_medicare_op = sum(medicare_payment_amt, na.rm = TRUE),
    claims_benres_op = sum(beneficiary_blood_deductible_amt + beneficiary_part_b_deductible_amt + beneficiary_part_b_coinsurance_amt, na.rm = TRUE),
    claims_pppymt_op = sum(primary_payer_paid_amt, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

reconcile <- beneficiary_all %>%
  select(beneficiary_id, reference_year,
         annual_medicare_reimb_ip, annual_beneficiary_resp_ip, annual_primary_payer_reimb_ip,
         annual_medicare_reimb_op, annual_beneficiary_resp_op, annual_primary_payer_reimb_op) %>%
  left_join(ip_by_bene_year, by = c("beneficiary_id", "reference_year")) %>%
  left_join(op_by_bene_year, by = c("beneficiary_id", "reference_year")) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("claims_"), ~ replace_na(.x, 0)))
tibble(
  component = c("Inpatient: Medicare reimbursement", "Inpatient: beneficiary responsibility",
                "Inpatient: primary payer", "Outpatient: Medicare reimbursement",
                "Outpatient: beneficiary responsibility", "Outpatient: primary payer"),
  beneficiary_file_total = c(sum(reconcile$annual_medicare_reimb_ip), sum(reconcile$annual_beneficiary_resp_ip),
                             sum(reconcile$annual_primary_payer_reimb_ip), sum(reconcile$annual_medicare_reimb_op),
                             sum(reconcile$annual_beneficiary_resp_op), sum(reconcile$annual_primary_payer_reimb_op)),
  claims_derived_total = c(sum(reconcile$claims_medicare_ip), sum(reconcile$claims_benres_ip),
                           sum(reconcile$claims_pppymt_ip), sum(reconcile$claims_medicare_op),
                           sum(reconcile$claims_benres_op), sum(reconcile$claims_pppymt_op))
) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
               caption = "Annual totals (Beneficiary file) vs. claims-derived totals, 2008-2010")
Annual totals (Beneficiary file) vs. claims-derived totals, 2008-2010

tol <- 0.005
tibble(
  component = c("Inpatient: Medicare reimbursement", "Inpatient: beneficiary responsibility",
                "Inpatient: primary payer", "Outpatient: Medicare reimbursement",
                "Outpatient: beneficiary responsibility", "Outpatient: primary payer"),
  beneficiary_years_differing = c(
    sum(abs(reconcile$annual_medicare_reimb_ip - reconcile$claims_medicare_ip) > tol, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(abs(reconcile$annual_beneficiary_resp_ip - reconcile$claims_benres_ip) > tol, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(abs(reconcile$annual_primary_payer_reimb_ip - reconcile$claims_pppymt_ip) > tol, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(abs(reconcile$annual_medicare_reimb_op - reconcile$claims_medicare_op) > tol, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(abs(reconcile$annual_beneficiary_resp_op - reconcile$claims_benres_op) > tol, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(abs(reconcile$annual_primary_payer_reimb_op - reconcile$claims_pppymt_op) > tol, na.rm = TRUE)),
  beneficiary_years_na_in_beneficiary_file = c(
    sum(is.na(reconcile$annual_medicare_reimb_ip)), sum(is.na(reconcile$annual_beneficiary_resp_ip)),
    sum(is.na(reconcile$annual_primary_payer_reimb_ip)), sum(is.na(reconcile$annual_medicare_reimb_op)),
    sum(is.na(reconcile$annual_beneficiary_resp_op)), sum(is.na(reconcile$annual_primary_payer_reimb_op)))
) %>%
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
               caption = "Beneficiary-years where the Beneficiary file value differs from the claims-derived value (tolerance of half a cent), and where it is NA")

Why they match — a finding worth flagging

Going in, the expectation (based on the DUG’s general synthesis methodology) was that these wouldn’t reconcile. Section 6 (“Methodology and Limitation”) of the Data User’s Guide describes each synthetic beneficiary starting from a real “seed,” with “the claims from the seed beneficiary… replaced with claims from other donor beneficiary claims sets” — donor substitution that would normally decouple a beneficiary’s summary totals from whatever claims ended up attached to their synthetic ID.

The actual result above is the opposite: an exact match. For all six components, the Beneficiary file’s annual total equals the claims-derived total (e.g., Medicare reimbursement of $648,456,860 for Inpatient and $209,292,350 for Outpatient, to the dollar). The reason is in the Codebook’s Appendix 2 (“List of Reimbursement Variables”) used to build the formulas in the table above: it defines MEDREIMB_IP, BENRES_IP, PPPYMT_IP, etc. as literal sums over the claim-level fields, not as an independently-donor-sourced figure. That strongly suggests CMS computed the six annual columns tested here (Inpatient and Outpatient; the three Carrier columns were not tested) after finalizing the synthetic claims for a given release, as a rollup of those exact synthetic claims — so they’re internally consistent with this extract’s Inpatient/Outpatient files by construction, not by coincidence.

This is a narrower guarantee than it might look, though: the donor substitution the DUG describes still applies to other Beneficiary fields — demographics, and especially the chronic-condition flags behind Sections 3–4 — which aren’t derived from the claims files the same way and carry no such reconciliation guarantee. CMS’s FAQ underscores that distinction directly: “much of the interdependence and co-variation among variables have been altered… conditional correlations… would not be reliable.” Read as: the dollar totals tie out; the relationships between conditions, demographics, and cost don’t necessarily.

Sources: CMS DE-SynPUF Data User’s Guide, Section 6 (“Methodology and Limitation”), Docs/synpuf_dug.pdf; CMS DE-SynPUF Codebook, Appendix 2 (“List of Reimbursement Variables”), Docs/de10_codebook.pdf; CMS DE-SynPUF FAQ, Docs/de10_faq.pdf.

6. Next steps

  • The reconciliation in Section 5 came back an exact match for Inpatient and Outpatient — the opposite of what the DUG’s general donor-substitution methodology predicted going in, and traceable instead to the Codebook’s Appendix 2 defining these annual fields as literal sums over this release’s claims. That guarantee is specific to the six annual reimbursement columns tested (Inpatient and Outpatient; the three Carrier columns were not tested), though — it says nothing about the chronic condition flags (Sections 3–4) or demographics, which follow the more general donor-substitution path the DUG describes and carry no such reconciliation guarantee.
  • cost_by_disease (Section 4) double/triple-counts claims across comorbid conditions by design (see that section) — don’t sum the claim-count columns (n_*) across rows expecting them to equal total claim counts.
  • Treat the condition prevalence and correlations (Section 3) and cost-by-disease breakdown (Section 4) as a demonstration of the pipeline and methodology, not as clinical or actuarial fact — both rest on relationships CMS’s own FAQ warns were altered by the disclosure-limitation synthesis.
  • Extending the reconciliation to Carrier would require re-deriving LINE_PRCSG_IND_CD-filtered sums from the raw Carrier files, since that column was dropped during cleaning — not done here since it wasn’t asked for, but the formulas are in Codebook Appendix 2 if needed later.
